headline: 1,608 hospitalised as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The death toll has risen to 256 this year, with over 84,000 patients admitted to hospitals nationwide since January.
details: Six people died of dengue in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The latest fatalities include two deaths in Dhaka South City Corporation, two in Rajshahi division, one in Khulna, and one in Barishal.
During the same 24-hour period, 1,608 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
Since January 1, a total of 84,369 dengue patients have been hospitalised nationwide, with 78,482 of them recovering.
Currently, 5,631 patients are still receiving treatment in hospitals across Bangladesh.

headline: 162* not out: Shai Hope leads Windies to record chase against India
summary: Despite a groin injury, skipper Shai Hope's monumental century orchestrated a five-wicket victory for the West Indies in the final ODI.
details: West Indies secured a consolation five-wicket victory over India in the final one-day international on Saturday, driven by skipper Shai Hope's unbeaten 162.
Hope overcame a groin injury and a sudden role change to open the batting after Jewel Andrew suffered a finger injury while fielding.
He led a record-breaking chase of 351, surpassing the West Indies' previous highest successful chase of 331 against Ireland in 2019.
India had posted a mammoth 351-7, powered by KL Rahul's career-best unconquered 129 and Rohit Sharma's breezy 92.
Hope's innings was a masterclass in stroke play, including a ferocious onslaught where he smashed 40 runs off his last 16 deliveries to seal the win with 10 balls to spare.
Hope credited his composure during the chase to advice from MS Dhoni, who told him that 'you always have more time than you think.'
Earlier in the match, Jayden Seales provided early breakthroughs by dismissing Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli in quick succession.
India's recovery was led by a 137-run partnership between Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad, who was dropped multiple times.
caption:
A record-breaking chase and a groin injury couldn't stop Shai Hope. 162* not out to sink India!

West Indies secured a consolation five-wicket victory over India in the final one-day international on Saturday, driven by skipper Shai Hope's unbeaten 162.

Hope overcame a groin injury and a sudden role change to open the batting after Jewel Andrew suffered a finger injury while fielding.

He led a record-breaking chase of 351, surpassing the West Indies' previous highest successful chase of 331 against Ireland in 2019.

India had posted a mammoth 351-7, powered by KL Rahul's career-best unconquered 129 and Rohit Sharma's breezy 92.

Hope's innings was a masterclass in stroke play, including a ferocious onslaught where he smashed 40 runs off his last 16 deliveries to seal the win with 10 balls to spare.

Hope credited his composure during the chase to advice from MS Dhoni, who told him that 'you always have more time than you think.'

Earlier in the match, Jayden Seales provided early breakthroughs by dismissing Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli in quick succession.

India's recovery was led by a 137-run partnership between Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad, who was dropped multiple times.
